pages.title: File:Hemakuta Hills.jpg

ObjectName.value: Hemakuta Hills

Categories.value: Virupaksha Temple|Self-published work|Tungabhadra River at Hampi|India photographs taken on 2020-12-31|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments missing SDC depicts|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments missing SDC location of creation|Files from competitions organized by West Bengal Wikimedians User Group|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments 2021|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments 2021 in India|Uploaded via Campaign:wlm-in-ka|Hemakuta Hill|Images from WLM 2021 India under review by Montage tool

ImageDescription.value:
The Myths of Hampi have it that it’s on this hill that Lord Siva (the god of destruction) did penance before marrying a local girl Pampa. Siva was impressed by her dedication for him and consent to marry her. On this it rained gold on this hill. Hema in Sanskrit language means gold. The name of the hill thus connects with this legend.

Hemakuta Hill is one among the best places in Hampi to see the sunrise and sunset.

This hill is sprinkled generously with a large number of temples, archways and pavilions.

See detail information at https://hampi.in/hemakuta-hill

Artist.value: Arjun Dharne

pages.title: File:Moola-Virupaksha-Temple-hampi.jpg

ObjectName.value: Moola-Virupaksha-Temple-hampi

Categories.value: Virupaksha Temple|Hemakuta temple hill complex|Self-published work|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments 2022 in India|India photographs taken on 2019-12-29|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments missing SDC depicts|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments missing SDC location of creation|Files from competitions organized by West Bengal Wikimedians User Group|Uploaded via Campaign:wlm-in-ka|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments 2022|Images from WLM 2022 India under review by Montage tool|South-Indian Images of Gods and Goddesses

ImageDescription.value:
The Moola Virupaksha temple, that exists on the slopes of the Hemakuta Hills predates the Virupaksha Temple. In fact the name itself (moola means origin or base) suggests of its antiquity.

As a part of Hemakuta Hill tour, on top of this hill many temples that predate the Vijayanagara period are found. Moola Virupaksha is towards the northern side of the slope that overlooks the Virupaksha Temple complex. There is a natural water spring (pond) right in front of this shrine.

The whitewashed cubical pillars of the open porch in the front is a great example of early Vijayanagara architecture. The original structure was is a partially dilapidated condition. But now what remains is the restored structure by the archeology department.

Right behind the Moola Virupaksha Temple, a cubical single chamber shrine of Hanuman is located. With the ruins make great silhouettes, the sunset shots from anywhere here is wonderful!
